:::intro{robot="anatomy" title="Look closer, when you want to"}
This page takes the sidebar apart to show how design decisions become the parts you see. You don't need it to use the sidebar: [its own page](../sidebar) has everything you need to build.

**Three easy ways in**

- Start with the drawing. Each number is one part, and the legend beside it names it.
- Want to know why a part looks the way it does? Its card follows the decision from the answer about the product, through the rule and the token, to what you see.
- Or start from a job, like Focus or Emphasis, and find every part that does it in the legend.

Come back whenever a part makes you wonder why.
:::

## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/dense-data/sidebar/card-1.png" alt="Panel: 1" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><b>Panel</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Elevation · What separates groups on the page? → Lines</div><div class="odv-am-why">Thin lines guide the eye along rows.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Color · Which color roles does it need? → Surface, text, action and status</div><div class="odv-am-why">Surface, text, action and status cover an operations tool.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.default</code><span>→</span><code>background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#FFFFFF · dark #161B23</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The base fill for content.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 17.28:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 16.26:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.raised, action.secondary. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.default.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.text.primary</code><span>→</span><code>label</code><span class="odv-am-val">#161B23 · dark #F7F8FA</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">Body text and headings.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.900: the strongest text step, 17.28:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.900: the strongest text step, 16.26:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.inverse. <section class="odv-am-card" id="part-3"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/dense-data/sidebar/card-3.png" alt="Menu button: 3" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><b>Menu button</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you act on it?">Affordance</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you hit it?">Reach</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Compact</div><div class="odv-am-why">Compact spacing shows more records.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · What is the smallest target? → Compact, for a pointer</div><div class="odv-am-why">Mouse and keyboard; compact targets are enough.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · How large is body text? → Small</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small body text fits more rows on the screen.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Slightly rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small corners keep dense rows straight.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For the smallest clickable thing, use size.control.compact. Don't use anything smaller.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For a link, use color.text.link. Don't use color.action.primary.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Links and buttons look different, so people know which one navigates.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For corners of buttons and inputs, use radius.control. Don't use radius.round.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small corners keep dense rows straight.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>size.control.default</code><span>→</span><code>menu-button.default.height</code><span class="odv-am-val">2rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. ## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `sidebar`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data sidebar`
